title: Single-node 300-case UI execution plan

fixture.origin: Existing synthetic 1M demonstration assembly; do not generate or import replacement data.
fixture.capture_offset_precision: capture_offset_seconds is an approximate display range, not exact timestamp arithmetic. Read the actual capture endpoints through execution_protocol.time_helpers; the current capture end is slightly below +720 seconds.

scope: Node workspace only. Local Route is an observed node projection, not the Fabric route tracer. Each record is an independent UI scenario; no case has been executed by this plan author.

baseline: Use an isolated browser tab on the existing /node workspace; confirm PE-A, the revision identity, 1,250,005 events, and 7,510 resources before the first case.
Reload the node page; ensure Durable review says Browser-only markers (Use browser only if needed). Never connect or write a durable workspace for this plan.

Click Reset, choose Separate, enable all layer chips, focus Selected time and press End; clear resource search, lane search and event search; choose All layers in the log, enable Normalized events only. Close overlays and wait for current timeline, resource, graph and dashboard reads to settle.

Restore default source presets: Unmatched CTF records and Unmatched external records enabled; EVPN ES signals and Programming errors disabled; remove only this plan's custom source lanes. Dashboard cases additionally use Reset layout.

Find resources through the actual Resources table or lane search. Record the rendered canonical data-resource-id before using a label; do not infer opaque IDs or treat identical labels in different tree branches as interchangeable.
settle_and_evidence: Perform steps in order through real UI controls. Except where a case explicitly overlaps actions, wait for local loading indicators to settle before the next step.

Record a separate outcome for every S ID: passed, failed, blocked, or not executed; include start/end time, exact inputs, observed canonical targets, DOM/screenshot evidence paths and any failure/recovery details.
Check expected assertions after the final settled render, including selected identity, focus, actual rows and visible counts. A completed click or HTTP 200 alone is not a pass.

For rapid/pending cases record whether an older request was actually pending. If natural timing misses the overlap, retain the ordinary sequential observation and mark the race assertion unexercised; do not claim a race pass. A controlled delay retry must be recorded separately with its delay and transport.
Capture local action-to-settled wall time where useful and identify browser automation overhead. Do not call that CPU time, heap growth or a natural-latency regression.

At the first failure capture the state before resetting, repeat that case once, and perform the documented next successful action; associate duplicates with one bug while preserving each case outcome.
If a required declared control/target is absent, mark that case blocked with evidence; do not substitute a different case or report a pass. Conditional complete-list branches are stated explicitly.
Read DOM attributes only to identify rendered UI controls and facts; do not call application functions, manipulate state, or invoke endpoints to simulate user operations.
time_helpers: Capture start is +0 s and capture end displays approximately +720 s. Selected time Home/End selects the actual dataset endpoints; End is slider value 1000000, not a promise of exactly +720.000 s.

Read exact capture boundaries through the UI: Selected time Home, then Topology > Absolute timestamp > Use selected moment gives capture_start_ns; repeat with Selected time End for capture_end_ns. Do not derive exact boundaries from the rounded 720.0-second display. Fill only the corresponding visible time input.

For exact event moments use the named event's actual UI selection/reveal. For a relative period fill Start offset and End offset, then use the specified Apply control; applying a range does not itself promise to move the selected moment.
Viewport Back/Forward means Back view/Forward view in the timeline toolbar, not browser document-history navigation.
jump_case_errata: Applies to S061-S090. These are plan corrections from the current frontend handlers, not execution results; every case remains planned_not_executed.

Ordinary event-hover Close dismisses the popup without clearing selection. Escape with timeline focus and no higher-priority overlay calls clearTimelineSelection: it clears event/source selection and range and resets the cursor. Keyboard cases record selection before Escape and then check the documented clear behavior, preserving both popup-dismissal and Escape coverage.

An event reveal may focus an exact mark or a cluster containing that UID. Verify the canonical resource and the target UID through the actual rendered evidence, rather than accepting a same-label instance. Reverse-jump cases still require a real exact event mark for their context-menu action; if needed obtain one through ordinary UI zoom before that step and record the extra move.

Selected time End means the actual capture endpoint, which may round to +720.0 s. Cursor interaction does not clear the selected event UID. Unchanged-End races must record value 1000000 immediately before the second End and preserve the event identity present after that newer interaction; they do not require an empty selection.

Toolbar Reveal in timeline first resolves the log selection and may reuse its query/range cache. Re-select through the UI before a pending case if needed for a fresh request. Distinguish selection resolution from later timeline refinement and record evidence of which older operation was pending at the newer action; absence of generic loading text is not sufficient. A missed overlap is unexercised, not a race pass; record controlled-delay retries separately.

Wait for timeline refinement and event detail before checking final focus; reverse jumps additionally wait for locate and virtual-page loading. Send follow-up keys to the current focus without implicitly focusing a locator, or focus retention has not been tested.

Hide a target through its Lanes checkbox before disabling its layer so both operations are exercised. Reverse reveal intentionally clears event search and layer filters. Viewport history uses Back view/Forward view and recorded windows; range selection is independent of the viewport, and navigation need not clear it.
